name: Mediation chain: Signal-API -> kappa -> SER (Pearl-Rubin counterfactual)
description: Operationalises the paper's load-bearing mediation claim (paper line 11 + line 101 + line 153): the Signal-API potency input is hypothesised to drive SER proximally through Kernel compilation efficiency kappa (Eq. 4). Paper's in-silico mediation analysis claims ~70% proportion mediated through kappa. This DAG sets up the Pearl-Rubin counterfactual decomposition (ACME + ADE) that Phase B's /api/v1/causal/mediation endpoint will compute via EconML DML mediation (D14 = gamma).
paper_reference: BOS_Paper1_JCP_FINAL.docx — paper line 11 (abstract claim of ~70% mediation through kappa); line 49-50 (kappa = CEA_post-M2 / Signal-API_BU_input, Eq. 4); line 101 (pre-registered in-silico mediation analysis, V14 wet-lab target); line 153 (Pearl / Rubin counterfactual mediation analysis on the Signal-API -> kappa -> SER pathway).

nodes.description: Normalized deconstruction rate. Downstream of kappa: higher Kernel priming -> better substrate access -> higher D'.
Normalized nitrogen recovery. Downstream of kappa via the larval growth response to better-primed substrate.
Final SER = sqrt(D' x G') (Eq. 3). The endpoint outcome for the mediation analysis.

edges.paper_quote: the Kernel compiles Signal-API potency S(tau) over a controlled residence time tau_M2 subject to first-order decay characterised by an effective rate constant k_decay (Eq. 5)
S(tau) = S_0 * exp(-k_decay * tau) (Eq. 5) ... tau_M2 <= ln(S_0/S_min)/k_decay (Eq. 6)
S(tau) = S_0 * exp(-k_decay * tau) — k_decay enters the exposure-time integral that determines effective CEA priming.

(implicit per paper line 11: 'Signal-API -> SER effect proximally through Kernel compilation efficiency kappa (~70% proportion mediated)'. CEA priming raises larval cellulolytic capacity, hence raises D'.)
(implicit: same priming pathway raises larval assimilation efficiency, hence raises G'.)
(direct effect path: Signal-API may affect SER not only through kappa; ADE captures this residual. ~30% of total effect per paper L11.)

intended_question: What is the proportion of the Signal-API total effect on SER mediated through kappa? Specifically: ACME (Average Causal Mediation Effect via kappa) versus ADE (Average Direct Effect bypassing kappa). Paper's pre-registered claim: ~70% proportion mediated. Phase B will compute via /api/v1/causal/mediation with method_family='dml' (D14 = gamma DML mediation).
estimator_recommendation: DML mediation (EconML / Farbmacher 2022 style); for the marginal ATE the same data supports LinearDML.
small_sample_warning: Paper line 101 explicitly notes the mediation analysis is 'in-silico, pre-registered for V14'. The 1000-iteration nonparametric bootstrap is on n=4 / arm — Phase B's /api/v1/causal/mediation MUST clamp evidence_level to 'planned' until V14 wet-lab data lands (n >> 4).
notes_for_user_review: DAG 002 is the highest-value of the three but also the riskiest. Two NODES (cea_post_m2, kappa) DO NOT EXIST in Phase A V5 schemas; B2b mediation endpoint will need data plumbing for these. Acknowledge before B1 starts so the requirements.txt / schema additions are scoped. The 'direct' edge from signal_activity_au -> d_prime is the paper's ADE channel; if user wants a pure full-mediation model (no direct effect, kappa is the only path), delete that edge.
